title: A reliable radio protocol
description: Turn lesson 7's fire-and-forget radio into a link that delivers every reading exactly once: sequence numbers, CRC-16, acks, retransmit with timeout and backoff, duplicate suppression.
outcome: You can show a lossy radio silently dropping readings in a seeded test, add stop-and-wait ARQ, and prove all readings arrive once, in order.

overview: The radio gives no delivery guarantee; you add one with numbered, checksummed frames, acks and retransmission, and you check it against seeded faults.

codeWalkthrough.title: crc16()
codeWalkthrough.detail: Bitwise CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE (poly 0x1021, init 0xFFFF): pure Python, so the same code runs in MicroPython and on the PC.

codeWalkthrough.title: encode()/decode()
codeWalkthrough.detail: Frame = kind:seq:payload:CRC4. decode() uses rpartition so the CRC is always the last field and returns None for any mismatch or parse error.

codeWalkthrough.title: receive() drains the queue
codeWalkthrough.detail: The radio queue holds 3 frames; reading until None keeps it from overflowing. ValueError (non-text packet) is counted as bad.

codeWalkthrough.title: send() is fire-and-forget
codeWalkthrough.detail: It increments tx and moves on: nothing ever learns that a frame was lost. This is the line the build task replaces.

codeWalkthrough.title: jline()
codeWalkthrough.detail: One JSON line with fixed key order; MicroPython has no guaranteed dict order, so keys are listed explicitly.

codeWalkthrough.title: solution.py pump()
codeWalkthrough.detail: One frame in flight with a deadline from running_time(); on timeout resend and double the timeout (100 -> 800 ms); after MAX_TRIES report gave_up and move on.

codeWalkthrough.title: solution.py on_data()
codeWalkthrough.detail: Ack every copy; deliver only seq >= expected; older copies count as dup. A jump forward is reported as gap.

# Lab 13 - tap counter + temperature reporter (BEFORE: a blocking loop).
# A press shorter than 3 s counts; holding A for 3 s or more clears the count.
# The loop polls the button, reads the sensor, then sleep()s for 1 s. It works
# when you press deliberately (hold ~1.5 s), but a quick 150 ms tap that starts
# and ends during the sleep is never seen: is_pressed() only looks at "now".
from microbit import *

SENSOR_MS = 1000           # one temperature line per second
LONG_PRESS_MS = 3000       # hold this long to clear the count


def new_state():
    return {"taps": 0, "down_since": None, "temp": None}


def poll_button(state, now):
    # edge detection on is_pressed(): we need the press DURATION, so polling
    # (not was_pressed) - and polling only works if it runs often enough
    down = button_a.is_pressed()
    if down and state["down_since"] is None:
        state["down_since"] = now                     # press started
    elif not down and state["down_since"] is not None:
        held = now - state["down_since"]
        state["down_since"] = None                    # press ended
        if held >= LONG_PRESS_MS:
            state["taps"] = 0
            print("clear")
        else:
            state["taps"] += 1
            print("tap", state["taps"])


def read_sensor(state, now):
    state["temp"] = temperature()
    print('{"t":%d,"temp":%d,"taps":%d}' % (now, state["temp"], state["taps"]))


def loop_once(state):
    now = running_time()
    poll_button(state, now)
    read_sensor(state, now)
    display.show(min(state["taps"], 9), wait=False)
    sleep(SENSOR_MS)       # BLOCKING: nothing else runs for 1 s


def main():
    print("tap counter ready")
    state = new_state()
    while True:
        loop_once(state)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

codeWalkthrough.title: poll_button(): edge detection on is_pressed()
codeWalkthrough.detail: Records when the press starts and ends; the length decides tap (< 3 s) or clear (>= 3 s). It only works if it runs more often than the shortest press.

codeWalkthrough.title: loop_once(): sleep(SENSOR_MS)
codeWalkthrough.detail: The blocking line in main.py: for 1 s nothing polls the button. A 150 ms tap inside it is never seen; no error is raised.

codeWalkthrough.detail: Each task is data: name, period, function, budget, next due time, error count, enabled flag.

codeWalkthrough.title: solution.py run_once()
codeWalkthrough.detail: For each task: skip if not due; log 'late' with missed periods if a whole period passed; run it inside try/except; time it; log 'overrun' if over budget; set the next due time in the future (missed periods skipped).

codeWalkthrough.title: solution.py safe_state()
codeWalkthrough.detail: Entered once after MAX_ERRORS consecutive failures: pin0 low, Image.NO, a JSON line naming the task; the scheduler then runs nothing.

codeWalkthrough.title: main(): while True: run_once()
codeWalkthrough.detail: No sleep in the loop: it only asks what is due. On the stub the test moves the clock 1 ms per pass.

"""Power budget MODEL for lab 14 (PC side). ESTIMATES, NOT MEASUREMENTS.

Runs a logger design (main.py or solution.py) on the stub for one simulated hour
with a fixed temperature trace, counts how long the board is awake vs in Deep
Sleep, and turns that into average current and battery life using the figures
below. Every figure has a source and a label; change them and re-run.

Run:  python budget.py            (Windows: py budget.py)
"""
import json
import os
import sys

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(HERE, "..", "..", "sim_stub"))
from labtest import load_lab  # noqa: E402
import microbit  # noqa: E402
import power  # noqa: E402

FIGURES = {
    # Board awake (On mode). UPPER BOUND: tech.microbit.org power-supply page,
    # "allow a worst case budget of 30mA for when all on-board peripherals are in use".
    "BOARD_ON_MA": 30.0,
    # Deep Sleep floor of the whole BOARD (interface MCU, regulator, sensors powered down,
    # pull-ups). BOARD SLEEP FLOOR, ASSUMPTION: no published figure; the model brackets it
    # at 0.05-0.5 mA and leads with the conservative end. Replace it with a measurement.
    "SLEEP_MA": 0.5,
    "SLEEP_MA_LOW": 0.05,
    # CHIP ONLY: nRF52833 PS "1.5 uA at 3 V in System ON mode, no RAM retention, wake on
    # RTC". A floor the board cannot beat - never quote it as the board's battery life.
    "CHIP_SLEEP_MA": 0.0015,
    # Awake time per Deep Sleep wake-up (read + log + back to sleep). ASSUMPTION: not
    # published, not measured here; measure it on a board before trusting the result.
    "ACTIVE_MS": 20,
    # 2 x AAA alkaline in series: Energizer E92 datasheet, 1,250 mAh rated at 25 mA to 0.8 V
    # (older revision EBC-1103I; the current manufacturer sheet gives capacity as a chart).
    "BATTERY_MAH": 1250.0,
}
REQUIRED_HOURS = 720           # the brief: one month on one set of batteries
MAX_DETECT_MS = 10000          # ...and notice a 1 C change within 10 s
HOUR_MS = 3600 * 1000
# temperature trace (C) for one hour: (from_ms, value). Same on every run.
TRACE = [(0, 20), (600000, 21), (610000, 22), (620000, 23), (630000, 24), (2400000, 20)]


def schedule_trace(trace):
    for t, value in trace:
        microbit._at(t, lambda v=value: microbit._inject_temperature(v))


def load_design(filename, source=None):
    if source is None:
        return load_lab(HERE, filename)
    import types
    microbit._reset()
    mod = types.ModuleType("lab14_variant")
    exec(compile(source, os.path.join(HERE, filename), "exec"), mod.__dict__)
    return mod


def run_design(filename, trace=TRACE, run_ms=HOUR_MS, source=None):
    lab = load_design(filename, source)
    schedule_trace(trace)
    state, samples = lab.new_state(), []
    while microbit.running_time() < run_ms:
        now = microbit.running_time()
        lab.loop_once(state)                  # the design's own loop body
        samples.append((now, state["last"]))
    slept = sum(ms for kind, _, ms in power.log if kind == "deep_sleep")
    # The last sleep can run past the window (e.g. an 8 s sleep started at 3,599,400 ms).
    # Clip to the window so the averages use exactly run_ms; that tail belongs to the next hour.
    overshoot = microbit.running_time() - run_ms
    return {"total_ms": run_ms, "slept_ms": slept - max(overshoot, 0),
            "wakeups": len(power.log), "samples": samples}


def detect_delays(samples, trace=TRACE):
    """ms from each trace change until a sample first shows the new value."""
    out = []
    for t, value in trace[1:]:
        seen = [s for s, v in samples if s >= t and v == value]
        out.append(seen[0] - t if seen else None)
    return out


def life_h(run, fig, sleep_ma):
    if run["wakeups"]:     # deep-sleep design: awake ACTIVE_MS per wake-up, asleep otherwise
        awake = min(run["wakeups"] * fig["ACTIVE_MS"], run["total_ms"])
    else:                  # never sleeps: awake the whole time
        awake = run["total_ms"]
    avg_ma = (awake * fig["BOARD_ON_MA"] + (run["total_ms"] - awake) * sleep_ma) / run["total_ms"]
    return awake, avg_ma, round(fig["BATTERY_MAH"] / avg_ma, 1)


def estimate(run, fig=FIGURES):
    # headline = BOARD estimate at the conservative sleep floor; the chip figure is only a bound
    awake, avg_ma, life = life_h(run, fig, fig["SLEEP_MA"])
    return {"awake_pct": round(100.0 * awake / run["total_ms"], 2), "avg_ma": round(avg_ma, 4),
            "life_h": life, "life_h_range": [life, life_h(run, fig, fig["SLEEP_MA_LOW"])[2]],
            "chip_only_bound_h": life_h(run, fig, fig["CHIP_SLEEP_MA"])[2]}


def report(filename, fig=FIGURES, trace=TRACE, source=None):
    run = run_design(filename, trace, source=source)
    est = estimate(run, fig)
    delays = detect_delays(run["samples"], trace)
    ok = est["life_h"] >= REQUIRED_HOURS and all(d is not None and d <= MAX_DETECT_MS for d in delays)
    line = dict(design=filename, samples=len(run["samples"]), wakeups=run["wakeups"],
                max_delay_ms=max(d for d in delays if d is not None), meets_brief=ok, **est)
    return json.dumps(line)             # observability: one JSON line per design


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print("figures (estimates, see sources in the code):", FIGURES)
    print("life_h = BOARD estimate at the conservative sleep floor; range = 0.5-0.05 mA floor;"
          " chip_only_bound_h is NOT a board figure")
    for name in ("main.py", "solution.py"):
        print(report(name))

"""Lab 15 - serial gateway on the PC (BEFORE hardening).

Reads the micro:bit's serial lines, turns each into a JSON message and forwards
it MQTT-style: one JSON line {"topic", "qos", "payload"} per reading. Works on a
clean transcript. On a real serial link (boot messages, a cable pulled
mid-line, a flipped bit) it either CRASHES on the first bad line or, worse,
forwards a wrong value: it never checks the length or the CRC.

Run:  python gateway.py --file serial.txt     (Windows: py gateway.py --file serial.txt)
"""
import argparse
import json
import sys

TOPIC = "microbit/{device}/telemetry"


class JsonLinesPublisher:
    """MQTT-style output without a broker: one JSON object per line."""

    def __init__(self, out=None):
        self.out = out or sys.stdout
        self.sent = []

    def publish(self, topic, payload, qos=1):
        msg = {"topic": topic, "qos": qos, "payload": payload}
        self.sent.append(msg)
        self.out.write(json.dumps(msg, sort_keys=True) + "\n")


def parse_line(line):
    body = line.strip()                     # "$LLL<payload>*CCCC"
    payload = body[4:].split("*")[0]        # trusts the format: no checks at all
    seq, temp, light = payload.split(",")
    return {"seq": int(seq), "temp": int(temp), "light": int(light)}


def run(lines, publisher, device="mb1"):
    for line in lines:
        if not line.strip():
            continue
        publisher.publish(TOPIC.format(device=device), parse_line(line))
    return publisher


def main(argv=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="naive serial -> JSON-lines gateway")
    ap.add_argument("--file", required=True, help="serial transcript (text)")
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
    with open(args.file, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as f:
        run(f, JsonLinesPublisher())


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

title: Close-sibling low-level code: a timer interrupt race in Rust
description: Rust + Embassy firmware for the micro:bit V2's nRF52833: a TIMER1 interrupt shares a counter with the main loop; show the lost-update race deterministically on the host, fix it with a critical section, and run the build under Renode's nRF52840 model as a close sibling (pending-ci).
outcome: You can explain and prove a read-modify-write race between an ISR and main code, fix it with a critical section, and state exactly what an emulator run on a sibling chip does and does not show.
environment: Local: Python 3.12 host model + static checks. pending-ci: Rust stable + thumbv7em-none-eabihf, embassy-executor 0.10.0, embassy-time 0.5.1, embassy-nrf 0.11.0 (feature nrf52833), cortex-m 0.7.6, Renode 1.17.0 (nRF52840 model).
overview: Below MicroPython, interrupts and main code share memory; a read-work-write that an interrupt can split loses data unless it is a critical section.

glossary.meaning: Interrupt service routine: code the hardware runs when an interrupt fires.
Code run with interrupts masked, so it cannot be split.
A write that overwrites a change made between our read and our write.
A different chip of the same family used for emulation; not the target.

concepts: Atomic types do not make read-then-write atomic.
Mask interrupts around shared read-modify-write; keep it short.
Emulation on a sibling checks the build and logic, not the board.

codeWalkthrough.title: TIMER1_BASE / reg_write()
codeWalkthrough.detail: Raw volatile register access at the nRF52833 PS addresses (TIMER1 0x40009000). The same addresses exist on the nRF52840 that Renode models.

codeWalkthrough.title: PENDING and ISR_TOTAL
codeWalkthrough.detail: PENDING is shared (ISR adds, main takes); ISR_TOTAL has a single writer (the ISR), so the report can check isr == consumed + pending + lost.

codeWalkthrough.title: #[interrupt] unsafe fn TIMER1()
codeWalkthrough.detail: Clears EVENTS_COMPARE[0] (else the IRQ re-fires at once), then adds 1. Inside the ISR load+store is safe: main code cannot preempt it.

codeWalkthrough.title: take(): the race
codeWalkthrough.detail: load, 2,000-cycle delay (~31 us at 64 MHz), store 0. A timer tick (every 100 us) inside the delay is overwritten. Two atomic operations are not one.

codeWalkthrough.title: start_timer1()
codeWalkthrough.detail: MODE timer, 32-bit, PRESCALER 4 (1 MHz), CC[0] 100 (100 us), SHORTS COMPARE0->CLEAR, INTENSET COMPARE0, NVIC priority 2 and enable, CLEAR + START.

codeWalkthrough.title: Uart (legacy UART0, P0.06)
codeWalkthrough.detail: ENABLE=4, PSEL.TXD=6, 115200 baud, byte by byte on EVENTS_TXDRDY - simple, and the mode Renode's model supports with easyDMA false.

codeWalkthrough.title: main(): snapshot in a critical section
codeWalkthrough.detail: Every 50 takes it reads ISR_TOTAL and PENDING together with interrupts masked and prints round/isr/consumed/pending/lost. fixed.rs changes only take().

buildTask.task: Fix take(): make read-work-write one critical section (critical_section::with in fixed.rs; mask/unmask in solution_model.py) so a tick that arrives meanwhile is deferred, not lost.

equivalents: C/C++ (CODAL, Zephyr): __disable_irq()/__enable_irq() or irq_lock(); C11 atomics for single variables.
RTIC (Rust): shared resources locked by priority ceiling.
MicroPython: micropython.schedule() / disable_irq() on ports that expose them.
inRealSystems: Drivers keep ISR work minimal and hand data to tasks through lock-free queues.
Races are found with deterministic replay/models and stress tests, because they rarely show on demand.
useWhen: Any data written by an ISR and read-modified-written elsewhere; prefer an atomic swap or a queue when it fits.
caution: This firmware is for the emulator and study. Flashing raw-register code to a real micro:bit V2 replaces MicroPython; reflash a .hex from python.microbit.org afterwards. Never run it on hardware that drives anything dangerous.
simulatorVsReal: Close sibling, not the target: Renode 1.17.0 has no nRF52833 platform, so the nRF52833 build runs on the nRF52840 model (same Cortex-M4F core and TIMER1/UART0/IRQ map, more flash/RAM, no micro:bit board: no LED matrix, buttons, sensors or interface MCU). Renode timing is virtual and block-based; the race is proven on the host. Nothing ran on a real micro:bit V2.

checkYourself.q: Why does AtomicU32 not prevent this race?
checkYourself.a: load and store are each atomic, but the ISR can run between them; the read-modify-write as a whole is not.

checkYourself.q: Why is a Renode run on the nRF52840 not a test of the micro:bit?
checkYourself.a: Different chip (memory, peripherals), no board hardware, virtual timing.

checkYourself.q: What is the cost of the critical section?
checkYourself.a: Interrupt latency for its length; longer than the timer period, interrupts merge.
